core_obligations: The easy direction (proof lines 2130-2132): a representable functor commutes with colimits by the definition of a colimit.

The construction (proof lines 2134-2172): assuming that the functor commutes with colimits, the author builds a candidate representing object as a colimit of subobjects generated by the images of the elements of the functor evaluated at the ambient object, using smallness to bound the subobjects, and defines the universal element by the compatible system of those elements.

The verification (proof lines 2173-2185): the induced map from the functor represented by the candidate into the given functor is shown to be an isomorphism, the inverse being obtained by sending an element to the induced morphism to the quotient constructed from the kernel of the universal map, the details of that inverse being omitted with that sentence written out.
proof_roadmap: Note that representable functors commute with colimits.
Build a candidate representing object as a colimit of small subobjects generated by the elements of the functor.
Verify the isomorphism with an explicit construction of the inverse.
difficulty_reason: The lemma is Brown representability for a Grothendieck abelian category: a functor on the opposite category into sets is representable exactly when it commutes with colimits (statement lines 2119-2128). The proof is a complete argument: the easy direction is the definition of a colimit (proof lines 2130-2132); the converse constructs a candidate representing object as a colimit of subobjects generated by the elements of the functor, which are small thanks to the cited smallness results (proof lines 2134-2172); and the verification that the represented functor is isomorphic to the given one is carried out by exhibiting the inverse on the quotient determined by the kernel of the universal map, with the details of that last check omitted in one sentence (proof lines 2173-2185). The non-formal content is the construction of the representing object and the inverse. The claim is H3.
